rows.text: Six years after COVID-19 killed millions, battered health systems, disrupted lives and brought the global economy to a virtual standstill, the world is still grappling with how we can prepare better for the next pandemic.
rows.title: The race to build a pandemic-proof world

rows.text: More than eight decades on, the UN General Assembly remains the place where the UN’s 193 Member States come together to debate the defining challenges of the day, from war and peace – to development, climate change and human rights.
rows.title: Why the UN General Assembly still matters

rows.text: Sitting in her Vienna office ahead of a pivotal UN gathering in Abu Dhabi, Monica Juma is focused on a simple reality: crime has evolved faster than many of the institutions designed to combat it.
rows.title: UN Crime Congress: Technology is transforming crime – and the response to it

rows.text: Khalilur Rahman took the gavel as President of the UN General Assembly's 81st session amid what he calls a crisis of confidence in the organization he has served – in one capacity or another – for 35 years.
rows.title: ‘Violence will only defer a problem’: UN Assembly President on trust, AI and lessons from the Rohingya crisis

rows.text: UN peacekeepers have increasingly been sent into places where there is no peace to keep – under resourced, outgunned and exposed to violence they are not equipped to counter. The Security Council meets this afternoon in New York to confront that problem, with Secretary-General António Guterres briefing ambassadors on how to close the gap.
rows.title: Security Council LIVE: UN peacekeeping under pressure

rows.text: For Benin, making progress on the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) has meant finding new ways to finance development.
rows.title: Less than 4 years from development goals deadline, progress shows what’s possible

rows.text: The deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has taken a disproportionate toll on women and girls, many of whom are on the frontlines caring for patients as well as their own families despite the high risk of infection.
rows.title: Women and girls pay high price in DR Congo Ebola outbreak

rows.text: Haiti is facing a worsening child malnutrition crisis, with an estimated 253,725 children aged 6 to 59 months projected to suffer from acute malnutrition between June 2026 and May 2027, new UN-backed analysis has revealed.
rows.title: Haiti: Child malnutrition crisis worsens amid escalating violence

rows.text: The catastrophic flooding that swept away entire villages in northern Nepal could occur again in the country or elsewhere in the Himalayas due to climate change.
rows.title: Nepal floods: ‘Apocalyptic’ destruction signals wider climate threat across Himalayas

rows.text: How do you make sense of a world facing interconnected crises, from poverty and hunger to climate change, if the facts are scattered across dozens of different places?
rows.title: New UN system platform puts millions of data points at users’ fingertips, says Guterres

rows.text: The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) is seeking to raise $97.5 million to protect 540,000 children and their families in Gaza and the West Bank from harsh winter conditions in the coming months.
rows.title: World News in Brief: Winter aid for Gaza, West Bank; Haiti food production; migrant deaths at sea; human rights funding

rows.text: At the current rate of progress, gender equality would take 171 years to achieve, a new UN report finds as institutions built to advance gains are being defunded and demobilised.
rows.title: Gender equality woefully off track, new UN report reveals

rows.text: The Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran confirmed that civilians in the country suffered serious human rights violations and “crimes against humanity committed by their government,” while finding "reasonable grounds" to believe that the United States committed “war crimes” in the context of its ongoing conflict with the Islamic Republic.
rows.title: UN fact-finding mission on Iran focuses on plight of civilians

rows.text: The UN Secretary-General has called for concerted action by governments, technology companies and civil society to stamp out hate speech, emphasizing that “its toxic message is spreading fast and striking deep”.
rows.title: Guterres calls for action as hate speech spreads across new platforms online

rows.text: The world is entering a period in which abnormal water supplies are becoming the norm, with river flows, groundwater and glaciers all showing signs of sustained disruption, the UN weather agency warned on Thursday.
rows.title: As freshwater reserves shrink, countries must prepare for a new water reality

rows.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing rapidly, raising questions about how societies and governments can capture its benefits while managing risks that often extend beyond national borders.
rows.title: Who should set the rules for AI? The UN is pushing for a safer digital future

rows.text: In Venezuela’s El Rodeo maximum security prison, some of those detained for political reasons are subject to forced intubation – and prolonged confinement in a sealed underground cistern.
rows.title: Repression continues in Venezuela in the face of ‘appalling’ human rights violations

rows.text: Ahead of the UN General Assembly’s high-level week, Secretary-General António Guterres said the world had entered “an era of deep uncertainty” and urged governments to embrace international cooperation to address global threats.
rows.title: AI, climate and conflicts top Guterres’s agenda ahead of General Assembly

rows.text: Since the Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021, the continuing presence of terrorist groups as well as rights violations against women and girls are a growing concern as the Security Council met Wednesday to hear latest developments, including from a civil society representative who said being born as a woman in the country “is a crime”. Follow full coverage here.
rows.title: Security Council LIVE: ‘Being a woman is a crime in Afghanistan,’ civil society briefer declares

rows.text: Activists, lawyers and others who cooperate with the United Nations on human rights continue to face intimidation and reprisals, according to a new report issued on Wednesday by the Secretary-General that calls for greater protection and accountability.
rows.title: UN report warns of reprisals against those who collaborate in defence of human rights

rows.text: Each September, New York becomes the centre of global diplomacy as presidents, prime ministers, ministers and diplomats from around the world gather at United Nations Headquarters.
rows.title: The world comes to New York: What’s at stake at UN General Assembly high-level week

rows.text: Following are UN Secretary-General António Guterres’ remarks to the Security Council debate on United Nations peacekeeping, today in New York:
rows.title: Put Peacemaking First, Forge New Partnerships with Host Countries, Secretary-General Urges at Security Council Debate on United Nations Peacekeeping

rows.text: Most United Nations peacekeeping missions now operate where peace remains elusive, Secretary-General António Guterres told the Security Council today, warning that blue helmets are increasingly being deployed amid active conflicts, shrinking budgets and rapidly evolving threats.
rows.title: Put Peacemaking First as United Nations Missions Face Growing Threats, Secretary-General Urges Security Council

rows.text: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres and Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) Director-General Qu Dongyu announced today their appointment of Luke J. Lindberg of the United States as Executive Director of the World Food Programme (WFP), to succeed Cindy H. McCain of the United States.
rows.title: Secretary-General Appoints Luke J. Lindberg of United States Executive Director, World Food Programme

rows.title: Sustainable Development Promises ‘Are Not Being Kept’, Secretary-General Warns at SDG Moment

rows.title: Secretary-General, at Launch of UN System Data Commons, Urges All to Join Single Gateway for Public Access to Trusted, Verified Data, Statistics

rows.text: According to a new World Meteorological Organization (WMO) report, rivers around the world recorded one of their driest years in more than 30 years. The findings point to a continuing decline in global freshwater reserves and ongoing glacier retreat.
rows.title: Daily Press Briefing by the Office of the Spokesperson for the Secretary-General

rows.text: The General Assembly today adopted a text to enable the high-level Palestinian delegation to participate virtually in the general debate next week, even as the representative of the United States said that the Palestinian Authority is subsidizing terrorists and using diplomatic theatre.
rows.title: General Assembly Adopts Resolution Allowing State of Palestine to Participate Virtually in High-level Debate
